summary: Legacy 2009-era ERP exposing customers, orders and a warehouse batch sync over a quirky REST API.

auth.notes: Client-credentials token. Docs claim expires_in 30 but tokens die after a few calls; re-authenticate on 401.

endpoints.description: Exchange client credentials for an access token

rules.text: Every endpoint returns HTTP 200 even on failure: check the `status` field; anything other than "OK" is a failure and the reason is in `message`.
rules.patternDescription: The API answers HTTP 200 for failed calls and reports the error in a body field.
rules.fix: Check the status/ok field on every response and raise its error message.

rules.text: Lists use `?pg=` (1-based, fixed page size 2). Keep fetching while `more` is true or you only get the first page.
rules.patternDescription: Fixed-size, 1-based page-number paging with a has-more flag instead of cursors or links.
rules.fix: Loop page numbers from 1 until the more/has_next flag is false and merge the results.

rules.text: Access tokens expire after a handful of calls regardless of expires_in. On 401, call /auth/token again and retry without surfacing the error.
rules.patternDescription: Auth tokens expire early or unpredictably and the API responds 401.
rules.fix: On 401, re-authenticate once and transparently retry the original call.

rules.text: Never call /sync during business hours (09:00-17:00 local): it locks the order tables and stops the warehouse floor.
rules.patternDescription: A heavy batch operation that must not run during business hours.
rules.fix: Refuse the call inside the blocked time window.
